evasion.title: Possible alt accounts
evasion.hint: Accounts that were seen on the same network address as this player. This is a hint, not proof: shared connections such as households or schools link unrelated players. Addresses are never shown.
evasion.empty: No other accounts shared an address with this player in the last {days} days.

evasion.weakNote: A link by the client setup alone is a weak hint, not proof: players who use the same modpack or launcher look alike. An address together with the client setup is the stronger signal.
evasion.weakOnly: Every account listed here shares only the client setup with this player. That is a weak hint, no proof: a modpack or launcher is used by many unrelated players.

apply.title: Apply template

apply.done: Applied step {step} of {count}; the score is now {after}.
apply.doneEscalated: Applied; the player is now permanently punished in {section}.

revoke.title: Revoke punishment in {section}
revoke.body: The active punishment in {section} ends and moves to the history.
revoke.resets: The punishment is permanent: the score in {section} is reset to the pardon score {pardon}.
revoke.doneReset: Revoked; the score in {section} is now {score}.

adjust.deltaHint: Negative lowers the score, positive raises it
adjust.invalidDelta: Enter a whole number other than 0.

adjust.doneEscalated: Score adjusted to {after}; the player is now permanently punished in {section}.

templates.title: Templates
templates.intro: Templates describe the punishments staff can apply. Each template lists escalation steps: the nth offence in its group uses the nth step.

delete.title: Delete template {key}?
delete.body: The template can no longer be applied. This cannot be undone.
delete.inUse: The template is still in use: punishments that came from it exist, so it cannot be deleted.

editor.windowHint: Optional; how long an offence counts towards the next step, e.g. 90d
editor.stepsHint: The first offence in the group uses step 1, the next step 2, and so on; the last step repeats.
editor.invalidCost: Enter a whole number of 0 or more.
editor.sectionHint: The ELO section this template charges and punishes in
editor.publicReasonHint: Shown on the public ban list when this template is applied. Admins only. No IP addresses, UUIDs or Ban IDs.
editor.advancedHint: Offences in the same escalation group count together: each new offence within the window moves one step up. Without a group the key is used and the default window applies. Most templates need neither.
editor.summaryRepeat: Further offences repeat the last step.
editor.noDuration: A kick or a warning has no duration; only its ELO cost applies.
editor.warnWindowHint: Optional; warnings older than this stop counting towards the next step, e.g. 30d. Empty: the escalation window applies.

sections.title: Sections
sections.intro: A section is an area with its own ELO score and thresholds. Crossing them punishes automatically: below the soft threshold temporarily, below the permanent threshold permanently.

disable.title: Disable section {key}?
disable.body: No new punishments or score changes are possible in a disabled section. Running punishments continue. You can enable it again by editing it.

editor.name: Name
editor.targetKindHint: What the server names below mean
editor.serviceWarning: A service name can belong to a different instance after a restart, so the ban follows the name, not the instance. Use a task or a group for lasting bans.
editor.serversHint: Comma-separated, * and ? as wildcards, e.g. bedwars-*, bw-?
editor.baseScoreHint: Where every player starts and recovers to
editor.pardonScoreHint: Score after a permanent punishment is revoked
editor.softThresholdHint: Optional; falling below it punishes temporarily
editor.permanentReasonHint: Shown to the player when the automatic permanent punishment applies
editor.enabledHint: Disabled sections accept no new punishments or score changes

vanillaImport.title: Import vanilla bans
vanillaImport.intro: Brings the bans of a vanilla server into Blackhole. Every imported ban is linked to a punishment template, so players see the template's reason in their language. Imported bans are enforced like any other punishment and cost no ELO. Use the preview first: it changes nothing.
vanillaImport.paste: or paste the contents of banned-players.json
vanillaImport.pasteHint: Pasted text is used instead of the chosen file. Files up to 1 MiB are accepted.
vanillaImport.ipsHint: IP bans are counted but not imported.
vanillaImport.tooLarge: The file is larger than 1 MiB. Split the list into several files and import them one after the other.
vanillaImport.previewAnnounce: Preview finished: {imported} would be imported, {skipped} skipped, {errors} with errors.
vanillaImport.importAnnounce: Import finished: {imported} imported, {skipped} skipped, {errors} with errors.
vanillaImport.confirmBody: The bans are created, linked to the template {template}, and take effect right away. They cost no ELO. An import cannot be undone as a whole; single bans can be revoked on the player page. Run the preview first if you have not.
vanillaImport.templateHint: Required. The ban gets this template's section and reason; the original reason stays visible to staff. Templates of mute sections are not offered.
vanillaImport.mappingHint: Link a reason of the file to another template than the one above. The reason must match the text in the file exactly.
vanillaImport.groupsCaption: Imported entries by original reason and the template they are linked to
vanillaImport.mapGroupFor: Use another template for the reason {reason}

importedPunishments.title: Imported punishments
importedPunishments.intro: Bans imported before imports needed a template have none, so players see the original reason untranslated. Choose a template per reason to link them. Only the template changes: no ELO, no duration, nothing else. Each change is written to the case.
importedPunishments.empty: Every imported punishment is linked to a template.
importedPunishments.applyFor: Link the punishments with the reason {reason} to the chosen template
importedPunishments.confirmBody: {count} imported punishments with the reason “{reason}” are linked to the template {template}. Players then see the template's reason. No score changes. Punishments that already have a template are left alone.

relayBanner.absent: {proxy} runs without SignedVelocity. Signed mutes there are enforced by disconnecting the muted player, not by cancelling the message. Install SignedVelocity on the proxy and on every backend server.
relayBanner.unknown: The SignedVelocity state of {proxy} is unknown: it has not reported recently.

cloudnetCatalogue.title: CloudNet catalogue
cloudnetCatalogue.intro: What the proxies report from CloudNet. Read-only; the section editor uses it for suggestions.
cloudnetCatalogue.empty: No CloudNet data has been reported yet. A proxy reports it after it starts and then on a regular schedule; reports expire after a while, so the data disappears when no proxy reports it.
cloudnetCatalogue.reportedUnknown: Time of the last report unknown.

header.heading: Case {id}
header.readOnly: You can read this case but not change it. Changing a case needs the moderator role.

header.conflict: Someone else changed this case in the meantime. Your change was not saved. Reload to see the current values.

notes.hint: Ctrl+Enter saves. Refer to players by their short id; no UUIDs or IP addresses.

banner.frozen: The Ban ID was marked leaked after the appeal was filed. The ticket is frozen: the player cannot write, staff still can.

conversation.formatHint: Markdown: **bold**, *italic*, ~~strike~~, `code`, > quote, - list, [link](https://...). Links open a warning page first. There is no preview.

lock.title: Ticket lock
lock.unknown: Not known yet. Locking or unlocking here shows the state.
lock.leak: The leak check locked this ticket. Staff cannot unlock it, and the player cannot write while it is locked.
lock.hint: A locked ticket takes no messages from the player. Staff can still write.

banner.incomplete: The transcript may be incomplete since {since}: no completeness check was recorded after the decision.
banner.lost: The Discord channel was deleted before the transcript was verified. The record may be incomplete since {since}.
banner.protocolMissing: The transcript is complete but no protocol is stored yet. The channel is not archived or deleted until it exists.

tickets.noProtocols: No protocol is stored for this case.

participants.confirmBody: The stored Discord account and display name are removed for good and the stored protocols are regenerated. Message text is removed separately.

banId.notIssued: This punishment has no Ban ID yet.
banId.hint: The Ban ID is the player's key to the appeal portal. It is shown only on request and is never stored in this browser.
banId.readOnly: Revealing the Ban ID needs the moderator role.
banId.leakTitle: Mark the Ban ID as leaked?
banId.leakBody: The player's portal sessions end, an unfiled right to appeal is forfeited and a filed ticket is frozen for the player. An administrator can reissue the Ban ID.
banId.reissueBody: A new Ban ID replaces the old one, which stops working at once. The leak is cleared. Reveal the new Ban ID to pass it on to the player.

transcript.title: Transcript export
transcript.hint: Downloads the conversation and the lifecycle of this case. Every export is recorded on the case.
transcript.includeNotesHint: Notes are left out unless this is set.

protocol.title: Stored appeal protocol
protocol.hint: The conversation of a decided appeal, stored when the decision was made. Opening or downloading a version is recorded on the case.
protocol.none: No appeal on this case has a stored protocol.
protocol.pending: A decided appeal has no protocol yet. It is created shortly after the decision and appears here by itself.
protocol.supersededHint: Replaced by a newer version of the same appeal. Purged versions are not listed.

punished.emptySearch: No player on this page matches the search.

notFound.body: This address does not belong to any page of the admin interface. It may have been moved or mistyped.

search.ambiguous: The id {id} matches {n} cases. Pick one.

appealConditions.title: Appeal terms
appealConditions.intro: Players read these conditions and confirm them before they file an appeal. Every save creates a new version; earlier versions are kept.
appealConditions.format: Plain text. A blank line starts a new paragraph, a line starting with "- " is a bullet.
appealConditions.conflict: The conditions were changed by someone else while you were editing. The current version is shown above; review it and save again.
appealConditions.tooLong: {count}: over the limit, shorten the text.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.intro: Every staff action, newest first. Read only: an entry is never changed here.

clientRules.title: Client rules
clientRules.intro: Rules over the client brand, mods, plugin channels, protocol version and commands. The proxy applies them; each rule can notify the team, deny the connection or the command, or apply a punishment template.
clientRules.honesty: Brand, mods and channels are chosen by the client and can be faked: a hit is a signal, not proof, and a miss proves nothing. Rules on them are a deterrent and a hint for the team. Start every rule with Notify, read the hit counts, and only then switch it to Deny or Punishment. Only the protocol version and commands are observed by the proxy itself.
clientRules.readOnly: Only administrators change rules. You can read the rules and their hits.
clientRules.empty: There are no client rules yet.

delete.title: Delete rule {key}
delete.body: The rule and its recorded hits are removed. Players already punished by it keep their punishment.

clientRules.acknowledged: Punishes on a value the client can fake (acknowledged)

kindHint.BRAND: The minecraft:brand text the client sends. It can be faked.
kindHint.MOD: A mod id from the legacy Forge mod list (Forge up to 1.12 only). It can be faked.
kindHint.CHANNEL: A plugin channel the client registered. It can be faked.
kindHint.PROTOCOL: The protocol version the proxy observes.
kindHint.COMMAND: The first word of a command line, also for commands that are forwarded to a server.

patternsHint.BRAND: Comma separated. * and ? work, case does not matter.
patternsHint.MOD: Comma separated mod ids, or id@version. * and ? work.
patternsHint.CHANNEL: Comma separated channel ids such as meteor-client:*.
patternsHint.COMMAND: Comma separated command words without the slash, for example op. A namespaced form such as minecraft:op is caught too.

negateHint.BRAND: Hit every known brand outside the list (an allowlist). A client that sends no brand is not hit.
negateHint.PROTOCOL: Hit every version outside the range (an allowlist).

actionHint.NOTIFY: Record the hit and tell the team. Nothing changes for the player. Use it first: the hit counts show what the rule would do.
actionHint.DENY: Also refuse the connection or the command, with the message below.
actionHint.TEMPLATE: Also apply a punishment template automatically. The player can appeal it like every automatic punishment.

editor.keyHint: Lower case letters, digits and hyphens; fixed once saved. The words catalogue and hits are reserved.
editor.name: Name
editor.spoofNote: The client controls this value and can fake it. A hit is a signal, not proof. Appeals are open for every automatic punishment.
editor.noSuggestions: No suggestions are available right now. Type the values yourself; the rule works the same.
editor.protocolHint: Protocol numbers, not Minecraft versions. One version: use the same number twice.
editor.invalidNumber: Enter a whole number, 0 or more.
editor.hideCommand: Hide the command from tab completion
editor.hideCommandHint: Cosmetic only: the command is still denied by the action below.
editor.noSections: There are no server sections. Add servers below, or create a server section first.
editor.targetKindHint: Optional, in addition to the sections. Patterns match the server name; the others are CloudNet names.
editor.serversHint: Comma separated server name patterns, for example lobby-*
editor.denyMessageHint: English, plain text, at most 200 characters. Empty uses a default.
editor.templateHint: Applied once while the player has an active punishment from this rule.
editor.punishWarning: This punishes on something the client chooses. Anybody can fake it, and a false hit punishes an innocent player. Use it only if you accept that.
editor.acknowledge: I know this value can be faked
editor.acknowledgeRequired: Confirm that you know the value can be faked.
editor.enabledHint: A disabled rule is not applied and takes no hits.

hits.title: Hits of {key}
hits.hint: Who triggered the rule, when and what the rule did. The values the client sent are never stored. Hits are deleted after a retention period; the count above stays.
hits.empty: No recorded hits (they expire after the retention period).

player.title: Client rule hits
player.hint: Rules this player triggered recently. The values the client sent are not stored.
player.empty: No client rule hits for this player.

leave.title: Leaving Blackhole
leave.heading: You are leaving Blackhole
leave.explain: Blackhole does not control this site. Check the address before you continue.
leave.invalid: This link is not a web address (http or https) and cannot be opened.

workspace.administrationHint: Templates, sections, client rules, staff accounts and imports

warn.title: Warn player
warn.intro: The template decides what the player gets: a warning, a kick or a punishment. A warning is shown in game and confirmed once.

kick.title: Kick {name}
kick.intro: Takes the player off the network, a server or a section. A kick is a moment, not a punishment: it is not active and cannot be undone.

reason.label: Reason
reason.hint: Shown to the player. 1 to 200 characters. Do not write a UUID, IP address or Ban ID.
reason.pii: The reason must not contain a UUID, IP address or Ban ID.

kick.waiting: Waiting for a proxy to answer...
kick.timedOut: No answer yet. Check the player history later.

mass.title: Mass kick
mass.intro: Kicks everybody from a server or a section in one audited action. It writes no punishment, case or ELO. It cannot be undone.
mass.confirmLabel: Type the target name to confirm

policy.title: VPN and hosting policy
policy.intro: What happens to a login from a VPN, hosting or proxy address. Only an administrator can change it.

allowList.title: Allow-list
allowList.intro: Exempt a player from the VPN and hosting policy for a while. The reason is kept with the exemption.
allowList.playerHint: The name is resolved to the player before the exemption is stored.
allowList.reasonRequired: Give a reason for the exemption. Submit stays disabled until then.

hits.title: VPN and hosting logins
hits.hint: Logins of this player from a VPN, hosting or proxy address. The address itself is not shown.
hits.empty: No VPN or hosting login was recorded for this player.
hits.allowListedNo: Not allow-listed at the last login.

rollback.title: Staff rollback
rollback.intro: Undoes what one staff member's punishments did in a time window, as a manual revoke would. Preview first: nothing changes until you confirm.

uuid.invalid: Enter the UUID with dashes, for example 069a79f4-44e9-4726-a5be-fca90e38aaf5.
uuid.label: Minecraft UUID
uuid.hint: The UUID of the unlinked in-game account, with dashes.

window.invalid: The end must be after the start.

rollback.expires: The preview expires at {time}. Start it before then.
rollback.nothing: Nothing matches this window. Nothing would change.

confirm.title: Roll back {name}?
confirm.counts: Revokes {revocable} punishments of {players} players. Kicks in the window: {kicks}.
confirm.manual: Each punishment is revoked as a manual revoke does, with you as the actor.

options.marks: Mark the {count} kicks as rolled back
options.marksHint: Only a note in the history. Kicks are never revoked and no ELO changes.
options.suspend: Remove the Minecraft link of this staff member
options.suspendHint: Done before the first punishment is revoked. The person can link again later.

reason.label: Reason
reason.hint: Shown in the audit trail. 1 to 500 characters.

done.CANCELLED: Cancelled. Items already revoked stay revoked.

error.selectorInvalid: This cannot be rolled back. Choose a staff member or an unlinked in-game account.
error.tooLarge: Too many punishments match. Narrow the window and preview again.

rollback.noStaff: No staff members are known yet.

badge.permissionNote: A permission removed while the player is offline keeps protecting until the next login.

refused.title: Protected player
refused.moderator: Only an administrator can apply a punishment to a protected player. Ask an administrator to decide.
refused.admin: As an administrator you can apply it anyway. The justification is recorded on the punishment.

override.label: Justification
override.hint: 1 to 500 characters. Do not write a UUID or IP address.

exemptionReviews.title: Exemption reviews
exemptionReviews.intro: Automatic punishments that were held back because the player is protected. Apply one with a justification, or dismiss it. Each review is decided once.

apply.title: Apply the held-back punishment
apply.intro: Places the punishment that was held back. The justification is recorded on it.

dismiss.title: Dismiss the review
dismiss.intro: Closes the review without a punishment. The score change stays.

justification.label: Justification
justification.hint: 1 to 500 characters. Do not write a UUID or IP address.

guard.title: Join guard
guard.intro: Decides who may join the network right now. The level in force is the stricter of the manual level and the level the unattended evaluator sets.

set.title: Set the manual level
set.hint: A lower level is not restricted. Every change is recorded.

guard.readOnly: Only moderators and admins can change the level.

settings.title: Unattended settings
settings.intro: Applied on every replica within about 30 seconds. Every save is recorded.
settings.thresholdHelp: From 5 to 240 minutes, whole minutes only.
settings.nightEnd: Night window ends (this time is not included)
settings.nextWindow: Next night window: {window}, in your time zone. Configured zone: {zone}.
settings.noNightWindow: No night window applies: the window is disabled.
settings.readOnly: Only administrators can change these settings.

problem.threshold: Enter a whole number of minutes from {min} to {max}.
problem.window: Start and end must be different times in HH:mm.

confirm.title: Set the unattended level to {level}?
confirm.body: While no staff member is online, only players the network knows may join. Set {level} only when unknown players must be kept out.

tile.title: Join guard
tile.bans: {n} active area ban | {n} active area bans

areaBans.title: Area bans
areaBans.intro: Autonomous systems (ASN) and countries whose connections are refused when they join.
areaBans.showInactiveHint: Lifted and expired bans stay in the history.

create.title: New area ban
create.intro: Refuses joins from one autonomous system or one country.

value.asnHint: The number, with or without AS

areaBans.reasonHint: Up to {max} characters. Stored with the ban.
areaBans.moderatorLimit: Moderators can ban for up to seven days.

lift.title: Lift area ban
lift.body: {value} is no longer refused once the ban is lifted. The ban stays in the history.

ipBans.title: IP bans
ipBans.intro: Holds one address or range at the firewall and on every proxy. The list shows the clear address, so it is for staff only.
ipBans.readOnly: You can read the IP bans. Creating and lifting them needs the moderator role.
ipBans.emptyLifted: No lifted or expired IP bans.

create.title: New IP ban
create.addressHint: One IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a CIDR range such as 203.0.113.0/24.
create.reasonHint: 1 to {max} characters. Staff will read it.
create.moderatorCap: Moderators may ban for at most 30 days.
create.permanentHint: Administrators only. The ban does not expire until it is lifted.

address.empty: Enter an address or a range.
address.invalid: Enter one IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a CIDR range such as 203.0.113.0/24.
address.tooWide: A range this wide is refused. IPv4 ranges need /16 or narrower, IPv6 ranges /32 or narrower.

duration.tooLong: A moderator may ban for at most 30 days.

errors.protected: This address is protected and cannot be banned.
errors.tooWide: This range is too wide to ban here.
errors.forbiddenDuration: A moderator may ban for at most 30 days. Ask an administrator for a longer or permanent ban.
errors.alreadyBanned: An active ban already holds this address or range.
errors.notActive: This ban is no longer active.

created.withWarnings: The IP ban was stored. Warning: {warnings}

lift.title: Lift the IP ban?
lift.body: The address is released at the firewall and on the proxies. The ban stays in the list as lifted.
